articleTitle: Impact of spatial hole burning on modulation response of vertical cavity surface emitting lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: It has been long known that spatial hole burning (SHB) has a profound influence on the characteristics of semiconductor lasers. SHB refers to the local depletion of the carrier density at points within the laser where the modal intensity is large. The depletion will reduce the overlap between the gain distribution and photon distribution for the lasing mode. This will in general lead to an increase of the average carrier density to maintain the threshold gain needed for lasing. It will also often lead to reduced side mode suppression since the gain carrier overlap may increase for a competing side mode with different intensity distribution than the main mode. In this paper we theoretically investigate the influence SHB has on the VCSEL modulation response.

articleTitle: Bragg reflection in waveguiding structure with nonperiodic radial and angular perturbation of permittivity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: In the present work oblique incidence of cylindrical waves on the waveguiding structure with two-dimensional (radial and angular) Bragg inhomogeneity of permittivity is considered. The permittivity of dielectric assumes to be presented in the form of a sum of spatial nonperiodically oscillating harmonics of perturbation. Amplitude and wavenumber of each harmonic smoothly Vary along radial coordinate. The perturbation as a function of the angular coordinate. is expressed in the form of a Fourier expansion.

articleTitle: Amplification in photonic crystal heterostructures with active media from doping superlattice layers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Computer simulation demonstrates that asymmetric photonic crystal heterostructures with defect layers provides lasing at two different wavelengths and in opposite output directions. The light field distribution and radiation transport in the photonic structures are strongly affected by the n-i-p-i layers periodicity, dispersion characteristics of the components, and. conditions at the interfaces. Described photonic crystal. heterostructures can be attractive for a wide variety of applications. In particular, they can be used as single-mode laser sources or amplifiers at the near-infrared spectral region.

articleTitle: Tunable optic filter based on liquid crystals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: We investigate the possibility of creating tunable optic filters that use liquid crystals as the operating element. The LC optical filter, a system of polarizer-anisotropic layer-analyzer, is based on the transmission dependence on passing light wavelength. The polarizers are located at an angle of 45/spl deg/ to the axis of the anisotropic layer and can be parallel or crossed.

articleTitle: Enhanced large signal laser modeling including thermal effects for analog communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Enhanced normalized laser rate equations suitable for large signal analyses and system level simulations are discussed. A large signal laser model including thermal effects and incorporating a modified laser gain formulation is presented. Symbolically defined devices (SDDs) implemented in the Hewlett Packard Advanced Design System (HP-ADS) are constructed using the proposed laser model. The effects of temperature on the transient response characteristics of 1.3 /spl mu/m InGaAsP/InP Fabry-Perot lasers are predicted using the SDD implementation.

articleTitle: Optical beam propagation in Ti:LiNbO/sub 3/ Mach-Zehnder modulator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: We simulate, numerically a waveguide Mach-Zehnder modulator, which is one of the most important components due to its application in high-bit-rate optical communication systems. It can be fabricated in z-cut lithium niobate, where the waveguides are formed by titanium diffusion in LiNbO/sub 3/ substrate. The device has optimized for high extinction ratio and low insertion loss with symmetric branches and arms using the beam propagation method. The method is used with a rather realistic model of the waveguide structure and applied. to z-cut configuration by including the effects of crystal anisotropy, Ti/sup 4+/ diffusion, and wavelength dispersion of the refractive index distribution.

articleTitle: Waveguide quasi-optical resonator for shaping uniform field
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: A theoretical model is proposed in the work. We derive the algorithm of calculation and give the obtained results on the intracavity shaping of an output beam with a uniform transverse intensity distribution of radiation in dielectric waveguide resonators. We give a basis for making an experimental sample of waveguide CO/sub 2/ laser with a radiation beam of a given type.

articleTitle: Nonlinear optical vortices in isotropic and anisotropic media
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The light field transmission in dielectric waveguides and optical fibers with various profiles of refractive index in the linear case has been explored. The nonlinear case of transmission has been considered with the help of envelope dynamics analysis of the flat wave packet dependent on the longitudinal coordinate and time or the complex amplitude dependent on three coordinates and time. Moreover, the vector field dependent on longitudinal coordinates and time has been described in an anisotropic medium. In the present paper, the vector field dependent on three coordinates and time in optical fibers with step and gradient refractive index profiles is considered.

articleTitle: Singular beams in highly elliptic twisted fibers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: From a mathematical point of view, the twisted fiber is an elliptic fiber in which the orientation of the major axis of the ellipse changes linearly with z. The authors describe the refractive index distribution, evaluate modes and polarization corrections for the cases of strong and weak twisting, discuss the topological phase and adiabatic tracking, and finally consider conversion of the angular momentum.

articleTitle: Optical pattern computers: classification by characteristics of optical fibre information-energy networks and prospect of its development
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Significant results in creation of separate optoelectronic units, blocks, simple devices and single back-end processors aimed at processing of images have been achieved. There is an important problem regarding their integration in a unified system of optoelectronic components and creation of integrated complex optoelectronic back-end processors, and as a result of optoelectronic computer systems, up to creation of the pattern computer.

articleTitle: Accordance of energy conservation law of differential equations which describe light propagation in nonabsorbent mediums of periodical structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Systems of linear differential equations with constant coefficients which describe light diffraction on transparent periodical mediums, obtained basing on Maxwell equations are presented in this work. Respective equations for H-mode-polarization and E-mode-polarization of electromagnetic waves, in which electric field strength of a wave is the main variable, were found. Equations for E-mode-polarization are more complicated than for H-mode-polarization by their structure. All equations were examined for accordance to energy conservation law, which means that divergence of Poynting-vector in a grating should equal zero. Solutions obtained from systems of equations for H-mode-polarization by parabolic approximation and by taking into account the second derivative were compared. We discovered that for thick gratings, if variable component of refraction index is less than 0.01, error at parabolic approximation is not considerable and it can be neglected.

articleTitle: Far-infrared gas-discharge laser
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The need for creation of a low cost and reliable submillimeter HCN laser for laboratory biomedical research has arisen. We have developed a submillimeter-wave gas-discharge HCN laser with a low frequency (LF) pumping of frequency 50 Hz specially designed for laboratory and clinical biomedical research.

articleTitle: Investigation of gamma radiation influence on rat blood erythrocytes in vivo and in vitro by holographic interference method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Plasmatic membranes are the main target of biological influence of different factors on a cell. Change of membrane structure results in a change of the elastic properties of membranes and can be a cause of morphological change of erythrocytes. This work is devoted to an investigation of the morphology of rat blood erythrocytes in vivo and in vitro under the influence of gamma-radiation. Use of an holographic interference microscope enables investigation of native specimens in real time.

articleTitle: Carrier transport in quantum dot structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: In the strict sense, the carrier capture or escape processes in QWs are consequences. The prime cause of these phenomena, as well as the reason of finite conductivity of solids existence, is the. carrier scattering on various deviation of the crystal lattice potential from an ideal periodic lattice potential. These deviations can be impurity atoms (ions), crystal boundaries, crystal lattice vibrations. If scattering concerning the existence of impurities one can eliminate by improvement of growth technologies that scattering caused by interplay between quasiparticles one cannot eliminate in principle, even at absolute zero temperature. Therefore, we focus our attention on electron-phonon interaction in. quantum dots.

articleTitle: Influence of thermal phase lattice on ultrashort pulses characteristics generated by DFDL
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The lasers with distributed feed-back on dyes (DFDL) are interest of as perspective source of ultra short pulses of radiation (USI), which are generated under nanoseconds duration of pumping. In view of the luminescence quantum yield, distinct from unity and presence of Stokes losses, the part of a pumping pulse energy of the DFDL passes in heat and, thus, during operation of DFDL in the active medium thermal phase periodic lattice (TFL) is formed apart from periodic structure of inversion population. The presence of TFL in active medium influences on the process of generation development and results in changing of the generation characteristics of USI. The fulfilled numerical researches have shown that TFL has strong influence on the regime of USI generation and their generation characteristic at nanosecond duration of excitation pulses. The TFL influence consists in increasing of positive feedback and results in an elongation of USI in 1.5 times (under dye molecules concentration C-5/spl middot/10/sup -3/ moles/l). The decrease of concentration essentially magnifies the TFL contribution in the value of positive feedback. The power of single USI is augmented with growth of positive feedback and it is caused by increase of efficiency of a depletion of a upper laser level of molecules of the active medium. It is shown that the decreases of the TFL contribution in positive feedback can be achieved by means of reducing of threshold energy of pump.

articleTitle: Use of self-calibration of photodiodes in colorimetric measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The first stage of development of a new kind of objective three-channel colorimeter is shown, namely the development of the principle of its working, which will allow to construct an inexpensive and accurate colorimeter which is well suited to industrial production. By using two photodiodes in each channel simultaneously, a simple and accurate set-up of three-channel colorimeter is possible.

articleTitle: Simulation of optical communication systems using direct and external modulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: In this work we present an analysis of the performance of optical communication systems using two types of modulation: direct and external. The analysis was based on mathematical models., which was implemented by using of PC SIMFO, a packet of simulation of optical systems developed by Photonic Technology Lab (LTF-UNICAMP). We used a nonlinear dispersive optical fiber and we optimized the optical source for this medium. By using both a Mach-Zehnder optical modulator and electro-absorption modulator we obtained external modulation by using a CW laser. The DFB semiconductor laser was used in the direct modulation. The receiver block used was the same for both types of modulators, and a PIN photodiode with a pre-amplifier circuit and an electrical filter were used to fabricate it. The performance of system was analyzed using the signal-noise ratio (SNR), bit error rate (BER) a and power penalty in the output of a receiver for both, direct and external modulation in a WDM link, considering many systemic parameters like frequency chirping; phase noise and cut-off frequency of 3rd order Butterworth filter.

articleTitle: Guided vortices in anisotropic twisted fibers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: As a model, the authors consider a round weakly guiding optical fiber with constant anisotropy induced along an axis chosen in a transverse cross-section of the fiber. They discuss modes and polarization corrections, topological phase and adiabatic tracking, and angular momentum conversion.

articleTitle: Calculation of photoreceiver devices of laser measurement systems by the R-function method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Previous work presented calculation by the R-function. method of created self-oscillator photoreceiver devices on the base of multiplier photocell, built-in to the semi-coaxial resonator with the range of frequencies from 100 to 1000 MHz. GOI photodetector devices were designed on the base of avalanche photodiode with microwave frequency 200 MHz for precision laser rangefinder systems In this work boundary value problem for the biconical resonator eigentones definition which consists from the cylindrical part and two frustum of the cones, generatrix, which makes an angle /spl theta/ with an axis z is considered.

articleTitle: New laser compounds emitting in green region under flashlamp excitation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: We report the development of a novel series of laser compounds and describe the performance of these materials. The new laser dyes are the derivatives of 7H-benzo[4,5]imidazo[1,2-c]chromeno[3,2-e]pyrimidine. They have been synthesized by condensation of 2-imino-3-(benzimidazolyl-2)-benzopyrans with aromatic aldehydes. The new compounds fluoresce in the green spectral region with high quantum yield. Efficient laser action of their methanol solutions has been obtained under flashlamp excitation with pulse width of 2.0 /spl mu/s (FWHM). The output laser radiation of these solutions in a non-selective cavity was in the 540-570 nm region.. The influence of molecular structure of investigated dyes on their fluorescence and laser characteristics are discussed.

articleTitle: Interference of laser beam in thin film on plane-parallel dielectric substrate at Rayleigh scattering
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Thin films on plane-parallel dielectric substrates represent waveguide or quasi-waveguide samples. The nonlinear formation effect in a periodic structure (PS) connected with the excitation of waveguide modes in the film due to initial Rayleigh scattering is known. In the present paper, it is shown that the role of Rayleigh scattering of light in the sample is much broader-the formation of periodic structures far outside the acting laser beam due to nonlinear effects of photoinduced change accumulation in the film is revealed. AgCl-Ag films (h/sub AgCl/ /spl ap/ 100 nm, h/sub Ag/ /spl ap/ 10 nm) evaporated in vacuum on plane-parallel glass substrates with thickness H = 1.35 mm were used in the experiment.

articleTitle: Dynamics of the dislocation reactions and optical self-recovering: single-axis crystals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: It is commonly supposed that optical vortices (screw or edge wavefront dislocations) are generated either by natural or artificial phase nonuniformity located on a light beam guide (or inside a laser cavity). A nonuniformly polarized beam is regarded as a field with a fine wave structure, bearing vector singularities such as disclinations, C-lines and L-surfaces without connection with optical vortices. Nevertheless, the fine polarization field structure can be transformed under certain conditions into typical phase singularities - optical vortices and vice versa. Moreover, the energy efficiencies of these transformations are considerably higher and constructions of corresponding devices are much simpler than those connected with the usual vortex generation. The aim of the given paper is an experimental and theoretical study of the singular field structure of a light beam in a single-axis crystal in order to reveal the physical mechanisms of polarization and phase transformations.

articleTitle: Polarization mode dispersion: causes of rise and influence on synchronous linear links parameters and structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Summary form only given. In the paper the polarization mode dispersion (PMD) phenomenon, the causes of its rise and the synchronous linear links maximum transfer rate and regeneration section length dependence upon PMD are considered. The available variants of PMD decrease by polarization transforming devices whose uses are proposed. Devices introducing losses are defined and the possibility of polarization phenomenon use for polarization channel division is considered.

articleTitle: Linear and nonlinear vortex properties of pulses in optical fiber
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The vast majority of fiber optic transmission information methods are based on pulse coding. The longitudinal envelope dynamics of various forms of pulses under linear and nonlinear conditions are well investigated. However, attention has not been paid to the influence of the transverse field structure on the pulse envelope dynamics. In this paper, the dynamics of the pulses in a rotationally symmetric medium with cross inhomogeneity of permeability (optical fiber) is considered. The slowly varying amplitudes method (SVA) has been used in the linear and nonlinear cases.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of optical pumped FIR lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: In the present work the opportunity of realizing of laser levels of inverse population is investigated during the bleaching of a saturated absorber. We have developed an original model describing features of laser dynamics for laser generation on rotary transitions of molecules of a saturated absorber, placed inside the resonator of a stationary CO/sub 2/ laser. The features of various regimes of laser oscillation are investigated and special attention is given to the opportunities of reception of the steady set of Q-modulated pulses.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of bandwidth expansion in erbium doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: A model is introduced in this paper and the effects is of nonlinear scattering on the amplifier gain are considered as well as other phenomena. The model can predict the gain value and the gain spectrum of amplifier. Various gain flattening methods are studied by numerical simulation of this model. The results of the simulation of the various configurations for gain flattening the EDFAs and approximate bandwidth of these methods will be detailed.

articleTitle: Measurements of low intensities laser radiation power on basis of trap detector
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The new variant a trap detect or design is shown. All of three detector photodiodes are connected in parallel. Absence of adjusting elements for each photodiode essentially simplifies of trap detector assembly and raises the mutual orientation stability of photodiodes during its operation. The developed variant a trap detector is intended for absolute value measurement, of the laser radiation power in an optical range with a relative error at a level of several tenths of percent.

articleTitle: Photometric method of measurement of absorption of high-reflective mirrors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The mirrors of optical laser systems, in which as a source of radiation the powerful lasers are used should have extreme low absorbing ability in order to prevent occurrence in them of thermal effects, which break spatial parameters of radiation and can result in destruction of optics. To resonator mirrors of powerful lasers even more rigid requirements are showed, as they are exposed to influence of intracavity radiation, which on density of energy considerably exceeds output radiation of the laser. In this work the development results of the absorption factor superficial measurement by a photometric method for the mirror coverings, including resonator mirrors of the powerful gas lasers are submitted.

articleTitle: Importance of as mole fraction on Auger recombination value in strained MQW GaInAsSb lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The theoretical analysis that was made shows the way of suppressing of Auger recombination and improving current characteristics of mid-IR long wavelength sources of laser radiation based on InGaAsSb/GaSb.

articleTitle: Factor of absorption efficiency of thin metal cylinder in microwave range
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The thin wire platinum bolometers together with cuts of the wave-guide were located in the enclosed chamber to reduce influence of airflows on coefficient of heat exchange of them with an environment. The bolometer resistance before and after feeding of UHF power was measured by simultaneous monitoring of the direct current through the bolometer.

articleTitle: Light processing of singular beams by optical wedge: natural traps of vortices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Recently, an unexpected way of optical vortex generation by natural phase objects, such as an optical wedge, has been discovered as a result of technological imperfections of cover glasses for microscopes. A Gaussian beam diffracted by the edge of a cover glass shapes its wavefront in the form of a straight helicoid, typical for an optical vortex. By variations of the wedge's height and the beam waist it can achieve a nearly ideal vortex form. A detuned optical circuit generates imperfect singular beams with a strong distortion of their wavefront and intensity distribution. The aim of this paper is to study the self-improvement process of the singular beam structure created by the detuned edge's optical system at the expense of capture of the singularity in the vortex trap.

articleTitle: Investigation of time delay trunk ATM-network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Summary form only given. The article presents ATM-technology on the level of access network and trunk network. Four reference customers' connection configurations and main conceptions of access net-work building based on optical fiber are analyzed. Article shows two methods for logical network topologies using effectiveness and network productivity calculation, theoretically defined these parameters influence on time delay in local and municipal networks. Time delay is defined for ATM-network using different types AAL protocols and its change in dependence upon network traffic trunk increase. As result the theoretical calculation is determined for the effectiveness of bus and ring topology with optical fiber use and for the effectiveness of equipped AAL protocols based on time delay for different multimedia applications.

articleTitle: About nature of coherence of light waves
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Starting from an understanding of precise representations of the nature of light, the authors discuss the concept of coherence of light waves. They explore the ideas of photons and quantum packages in relation to the characteristics of coherence.

articleTitle: Characteristic properties of thermal regime in small diameter gas discharge tube
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Machine solutions of the closed equations system for determination the intensity of the longitudinal electric field, electronic temperature and the temperature of the working gas that are stated in plasma of gas discharge of the one-component gas mixture in the case of diffusion regime of the glowing discharge are presented. Taking into consideration the wall sheath of space charge the thermal regime in a small gas discharge tube is examined.

articleTitle: Fiber refractive index profile determination from the measured near field intensity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The main geometric parameters of optical fibers, bandwidth, mode field diameter, condition of single mode propagation, inter-waveguide coupling coefficient can be, related with their refractive index profile. In determination these parameters it's necessary to have the precision method for refractive index profile measurement. The optic fiber small geometric sizes and low difference of refractive index is caused by this problem realization difficulty.

articleTitle: Analytical approach to resonance diffraction under Wood anomalies existence for crossed gratings
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The results of both numerical and analytical examination of Wood-type anomalies for diffraction at crossed gratings are presented. The general reflective properties of the double periodic structures formed by modulation of the electromagnetic properties of the surface are investigated. The dependence of the reflection coefficients on the grating orientations, periods, form and modulation magnitudes, and on the angle of incidence is examined. In particular, it is shown that the total suppression of the specular reflection (TSSR) of an arbitrary polarized incident wave is possible for normal incidence and corresponding specific values of the gratings parameters are found.

articleTitle: Laser beam diagnostics with scattered radiation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: When backscattering is used for analysis the state of the surface becomes important. Unfortunately, the monitoring of the wire surface in an optical range during is manufacturing is practically impossible. Therefore investigation of the scattering diagram. was done experimentally to define the scale of distortions and to find the possibility of using back scattering for main types of sensors. In our experimental setup we used a continuous Nd:YAG laser and strong bounding beam with diaphragms at the output to create the quasi-uniform intensity distribution.

articleTitle: Simple laser interferometers for laser optics testing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: A simple laser interferometer for laser and astronomical optics testing is proposed. It consists of a small concave or convex mirror, a gas laser, a semitransparent flat mirror and concave mirror or a system under test, and a register equipment. The interferometer works the, following way: laser beam is reflected by concave or convex micromirror and then it is directed to the semitransparent flat mirror, and to the mirror or the system under test. The light reflected by the flat mirror of the interferometer is the reference wave, the light, reflected by the mirror of the system under test is imperfect wave to be tested. The reference wave and the imperfect wave are recombined to produce a system of Twyman-Green fringes in a receiving screen or in a register equipment to obtain interferograms. It is possible also to test any concave ellipsoidal mirror by properly shifting of the semitransparent flat mirror along the optical axis of the mirror under test. By the way, a spherical surface is a spherical case of an ellipsoid. Hyperboloidal mirror may be tested by means of the incorporation of a null corrector, for example Offner type one. The interferometer was successfully manufactured and tested at the Crimean Astrophysical Observatory.

articleTitle: Investigation of time delay trunk ATM-network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The article presents ATM-technology on the level of access network and trunk network. Four reference customers connection configurations and main conceptions of access network building based on optical fiber are analyzed. This article shows two methods for logical network topologies using effectiveness and, network productivity calculation, and theoretically defined these parameters that influence on time delay in local and municipal networks. Time delay is defined for ATM-networks using different types of AAL protocols and its change in dependence upon network traffic trunk increase. As a result topology with optical fiber use and the effectiveness of equipped AAL protocols based on time delay for different multimedia applications is found.

articleTitle: Laser beam shape invariance parameters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Quantitative characterization of laser beam intensity distribution shape is of great importance for beams comparison, to analyze their transformation along the propagation path or as criteria for DOE synthesis. One important application is distinguishing between the near field, Fresnel and Fraunhofer diffraction zones. For laser beams, such parameters have to be based on measured intensity distribution due to phase front measurements being too difficult in practice. The most general approach to the definition of Shape Invariance Error (SIE) has to be used. The well known Gelder norms of vectors or matrices for SIE calculation are proposed here. As examples, SIE for 3D-propagation of typical beams are considered. These parameters can be used as criteria in beam shape and technology process monitoring, resonator optimization to form beams with specified shape, optical systems development and optimization, etc. The fixed SIE level Shape Invariance Range (SIR) is an effective tool for comparison of laser beams or optical elements.

articleTitle: Finite difference method for research of wave beam propagation in nonlinear inhomogeneous lossy media
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: This work originates from the need to construct an automatic solution for the problems of Gaussian beam (GB) propagation in various media and scattering on arbitrary smooth bodies. The solution is obtained using a finite difference (FD) technique applied to the complex eikonal equation and (optionally) to the transport equations. The authors consider the ray-tracing technique, which is very simple and easily realizable numerically. The eikonal equation has been solved using complex rays tracing. Numerical solution of the eikonal equation allows the dependence of the refraction coefficient on the coordinates and the amplitude to be taken into account easily.

articleTitle: Research of special features of second harmonic generation of tunable radiation from flashlamp-pumped dye lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The estimation of allowable beam loading of nonlinear optical crystals can be carried out on energy density of the focused laser radiation it microsecond pulses of radiation. This magnitude should d not exceed 15-20 J/cm/sup 2/ for KH/sub 2/PO/sub 4/ (KDP) crystals. It is necessary to apply crystals of large length that promotes rather high SHG efficiency and long-term operation of system under conditions that are typical for flash lamp pumped (FLP) dye lasers (DL). There the requirements were determined to the main parameter's of FLP DL radiation that provide effective SHG by use of known nonlinear-optical crystals.

articleTitle: Wide-aperture electrodischarge excimer laser
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: With the purpose of reception of energy of generation 1-5 J the breadboard model of the wide aperture electrodischarge XeCl-laser with a UV preionization was created with aperture 6 x 3 cm/sup 2/. The construction of the laser chamber and circuitry of system of excitation of the laser is submitted.

articleTitle: Research of possible improvement of lidar potential performance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: A possibility to reduce the influence of the turbulent atmosphere on the potential performance of lidar instruments is studied. It is shown that the improvement can be achieved by using adaptive telescopes, which compensate the turbulent distortions of optical signals in each sensing cycle. This facilitates an increase of the signal to noise ratio in the output of the photoreceiver, and, therefore, an improvement in the instrument performance.

articleTitle: Outcomes of researches stabilized He-Ne/I/sub 2/-lasers, included in state measurement standard of unit of length
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Planned work on service of stabilized He-Ne//sup 1.27/I/sub 2/ lasers included in the state measurement standard of a unit of length was conducted. The purpose of this study was to find a definition of intercarrier frequencies between lasers. Stability and reproducibility of laser radiation frequencies, temperature, and power shifts of radiated frequencies of stabilized helium-neon lasers were obtained.

articleTitle: 2D computer modeling of waveguiding in 2D photonic crystals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Two-dimensional computer modeling of waveguiding in 2D electromagnetic (photonic) crystals is carried out using the 2D finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method (leapfrog technique) with second order Mur's absorbing boundary conditions. The Maxwell equations in electromagnetic (photonic) crystals are derived. The results of computer modeling are presented.

articleTitle: Pulse-periodic source of tunable UV radiation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: We report the experimental results that were received from tunable source of the UV-radiation based on the flash lamp pumped (FLP) dye laser (DL) which operated in pulse periodic mode.. This source. was developed for biological and medical researches in the 260-330 nm range.

articleTitle: Some properties of quasisteady-state discharges in power excimer lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: One of features of volume discharges - presence of layer of a cathode voltage drop, due to which in stable stationary conditions of uniform burning on the area receiving electrons is provided from the cathode field in a discharge column. A voltage drop and size of cathode field are fixed so that the requirements of self-maintenance, that is discharge due to ionization processes in gas and secondary processes on the cathode are carried out.

articleTitle: Application of principles of object-oriented programming for simulation of semiconductor injection lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The processes of simulation of semiconductor injection lasers by using principles of object-oriented programming (OOP) are considered. The opportunity to account for all the spectrum of existing injection lasers is shown to depend on laser design and laser spectral characteristics. In this work, the hierarchy of classes of semiconductor injection lasers with use of the basic principles OOP such, as inheritance, encapsulation and polymorphism is constructed.

articleTitle: Holographic visocontrastometry
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: A new holographic visocontrastometry method is proposed. This method is based on using the multi-angle hologram instead of the number of test gratings. It is proposed to use the dynamic hologram for distortion compensation for test grating images projected on an eye retina caused by different defects of the eye media. The method not only simplifies ophthalmology disease diagnosis process but also provides a unique possibility of examination and treatment in the cases of such serious diseases as leukoma, cataracts, and opacity of the vitreous body.

articleTitle: Abnormal spectral efficiency of generation lasers dyes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: We show generation characteristics of some known dyes coumarin, rhodamine and oxazine, and also again synthesized coumarin connections from spectral structure of radiation pumped at excitation by pulses of microsecond duration abnormal dependence of efficiency of generation, and also spectral characteristics on length of wave were was found out. Abnormal generation characteristics dependence of dyes coumarin, rhodamine, and oxazine and other classes from spectral structure and duration of stimulating radiation which is connected to structure of spectra excited S-S absorption and spectra of absorption short time living products of photoexcitation are found out.

articleTitle: Energy release in processing of tantalum with nanosecond Nd:glass laser pulse
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The total energy involved in the interaction of nanosecond Nd:glass laser pulses with tantalum in oxygen at pressures of 760 Torr and 1 Torr has been investigated experimentally in the range of laser fluences between 0.05 and 6 J/cm/sup 2/. It was found that for interactions in the range of laser fluences below 0.08 J/cm/sup 2/, the total energy is equal to the energy of the laser pulse. At laser fluences above 0.08 J/cm/sup 2/, a release of additional energy was observed at both oxygen pressures. The estimated contribution of chemical energy produced by the formation of tantalum pentoxide is not sufficient for the explanation of the observed additional energy release.

articleTitle: All-optical switching based on grating written photorefractive slab/fiber waveguide coupler
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: A slab/fiber geometry will be investigated for all-optical-switching. Here, the slab is a thin layer of polymer or crystal, showing a moderate photorefractive effect, attached to the core of optical fiber. The thickness of the slab is just enough to accommodate the refractive index change depth of the grating which is written externally via an intensity distribution of two coherent beam interference.

articleTitle: Controlled pulsed laser-induced microcombustion of solid fuels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: A microcombustion produced by the irradiation of coke and coal with nanosecond Nd:glass laser pulses in air at atmospheric pressure has been investigated experimentally. It was found that microcombustion occurs in a laser-ablated fuel, which is heated and ignited by the laser radiation. The irradiated fuel sample is not affected by burning. On the basis of the measured and calculated values of the thermal energy produced by the laser-driven microcombustion, it was demonstrated that complete combustion of the ablated material occurs. The amount of ablated fuel and, correspondingly, the amount of thermal energy produced by the laser-driven microcombustion depend on laser pulse parameters that allow the laser microcombustion to be controlled by means of changing laser beam parameters.

articleTitle: Polarization-mode dispersion in single mode waveguide of telecommunication system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: We investigate the causes of polarisation mode dispersion (PMD) in single mode fibre lightguide and describe it main statistical performance for strong mode coupling, which observed in long-distance telecommunication system.

articleTitle: Angular momentum evolution of optical vortices in anisotropic fibers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The model, spin-orbit interaction, modes and polarization corrections for optical vortices in anisotropic fibers are presented.

articleTitle: Temperature characteristics measurement at expense of single vortex recovering
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The subject of this paper is to elucidate the propagation process of a combined singular beam in a real consumer fiber, the fusion. and decay events of coupled vortices and the self-recovery of the free optical vortex after the lens system located at the fiber output. We also discuss the opportunity to design a fiber-vortex temperature sensor on the basis of these processes.

articleTitle: Specialities of laser homodyne vibrometers work in pulse mode
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The results of theoretical and experimental researches of laser homodyne vibrometer in the pulse mode at small ratio of signal to noise are given and the ways of creation of conditions for effective work are offered in the annotation.

articleTitle: Conversion of singular beams in free space: high-effective optical traps
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Earlier investigations have shown that ordinary cover glasses for microscopes have small areas near a plate edge with a sharp surface profile that transform an initial fundamental Gaussian beam into a steady singular beam with the central zero at its axis. We have called such a glass area an optical vortex trap. In this paper, we study experimentally these singular beams in view of the optical traps of large microparticles in the near-IR spectrum area and discuss capture-particle theory in relation to such singular beams.

articleTitle: Measuring of laser power at low pressure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The obtained results confirms that thin wires can be used as sensors for laser beam diagnostics at pressure from 1 bar up to 20-50 mbar without additional corrections. After that correction of the temperature dependence has to be done taking into account calculated or measured temperature distribution. With such the correction thin wire grids may be used for beam diagnostics even in high vacuum.

articleTitle: Single mode conditions in photonic crystal vertical cavity surface-emitting lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The theoretical aspect of single transversal mode operation in a photonic crystal surface emitting laser (PCSEL) is presented. First generalized VB diagrams for the holey waveguiding laser structure based on the effective refractive index of the photonic crystal cladding region are presented and discussed. In this paper, we also discuss advantages and drawbacks of mode stabilization due to light localization with photonic crystal defect.

articleTitle: Powerful light pulses forming in passive cavities
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Possibilities of short light pulses forming using a controllable Fabry-Perot interferometer based on an optical fiber were considered. This controllable interferometer consists of four similar Bragg's gratings which are set in a certain order on a fiber and which produce two interferometers. If the length of the first interferometer is 10m and the length of the second one is 67mm, gratings reflection for Bragg wavelength equal 0.99 and when the power of 100 W comes to such an interferometer in a fiber then it is possible to obtain 10/sup 6/ W power pulses. Light pulses are formed due to reduction of gratings reflection to null by electric field short pulse influence which is applied to the gratings by means of the value which is enough to produce the necessary change of optical fiber refraction index.

articleTitle: Absolute power meters of optical radiation for the state measurement standards of Ukraine
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: One of ways of a volume expansion and increase of measurement accuracy is the application of an absolute meter of optical power on the basis a gangway of the detector. We suppose to apply such meter of power separately for visible and to infra-red wavelength band. For this purpose we suppose to mount an input of an optical detector the changeable adapter permitting to include meter connectors of optical cables of different standards and their modifications. The characteristics of the dependence of an output signal of the photodiode from a wavelength of the received signal for different photosensing materials are shown.

articleTitle: "Superlocalization" of nonlinear waves in periodic layered and modulated structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The localization of nonlinear waves propagating in an anharmonic medium along an infinite array of identical plane-parallel defect layers (optical waveguides) is investigated. An effective analytical method of solving this problem is proposed in the limit of weak coupling of the waveguides. It is shown that the effective interaction of defect layers (waveguides) depends on wave parameters. "Superlocalization" (formation of a "supersoliton") of the wave flux in periodic layered or waveguide structures perpendicular to the direction of its propagation is theoretically described.

articleTitle: Generation of code sequences for asynchronous optical CDMA systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: In this paper two families of optical orthogonal codes (OOCs) are algebraically designed by using the Galois field. The first family of codes has nonideal auto band cross-correlation /spl lambda//sub a/=1, /spl lambda//sub c/=2 properties. The second family of codes has ideal auto band cross-correlation /spl lambda//sub a/=1, /spl lambda//sub c/=1 properties. It is shown that the p-1 codes exist for every prime p forming a family of (v, /spl omega/, /spl lambda//sub a/, /spl lambda//sub c/) OOCs. These codes may serve as many as p-1 different users in the fiber-optic code division mutiple access system. We also compare their performance with previous known codes. We present examples of the constructed codes. The algebraic OOCs being proposed in this paper find applications in asynchronous OCDMA systems.

articleTitle: Application of Monte-Carlo method for losses account in elements of integral-optical systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Use of the Monte Carlo method for definition of loss level in integrated-optical devices is offered in this work. An optical waveguide losses calculation example curve is given. Limits of the method's applicability are pointed out.

articleTitle: Investigation of complex waves in semiconducting periodic structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The electrodynamical properties of complex plasma polaritons are investigated in the present work. Complex waves are waves having a complex wave vector, even in the absence of dissipative processes. The imaginary part of the wave vector of complex plasma polaritons in a medium with translation symmetry is much greater than the real one. This is due to the fact that the dielectric permittivity of a plasma-like medium can be negative at plasma frequencies. An infinite periodic structure formed by alternating semiconductor layers of thickness d/sub 1/ and d/sub 2/ is considered.

articleTitle: Total suppression of specular reflection of arbitrary polarized radiation caused by excitation of surface polariton
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Summary form only given. The effect of total suppression of specular reflection (TSSR) was first examined TM polarization in an in-plane geometry. It is caused by transformation of the incident light in the surface electromagnetic wave (surface plasmon-polariton, SPP) due to diffraction at a shallow grating. For out-of-plane (conical) diffraction, resonance excitation of SPP leads to great changes in the intensity and polarization of the specular reflected wave. In this work, it is shown that, if we are dealing with gratings formed by modulation of the surface impedance, then there exists a specific configuration allowing one to observe TSSR for an arbitrary polarized incident wave.

articleTitle: Influence of discharge parameters on space charge in narrow gas discharge tubes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The expression for magnitude of a volume charge on an axis of a positive column of a glow discharge is obtained depending on parameters of discharge. The extreme dependence of a uncompensated positive charge at centre of a gas discharge tube from a density of electrons on an axis is established. The electronic temperature and gas pressure determine location of extremely (maxima) point.

articleTitle: System of interferential signals automatized processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The developed system of interferential signals automated processing and the proposed methodic on interferential traces recognition, based on gradient calculation, provide the effective and quick calculation of roughness on the end face of optical connector ferrules in optical fiber communication system.

articleTitle: Dependence of double-resonance diffraction peculiarities on impedance grating parameters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Summary form only given. We present analysis of (-1, 1) and (-2, 1) resonance diffraction for in-plane geometry at an impedance grating of arbitrary form. The consideration is based on improved results of previous work (Kats and Spevak, 1998; Balakhonova et al., 2001). In the vicinity of close resonance, we provide expansion with respect to small deviations from the unshifted resonance point. We present results in a scaled form that possess universality, and therefore the specific parameters of the grating and surface material define only the position of the resonance and the tails of the resonance curve.

articleTitle: Quasioptical laser resonator on the basis of a metal waveguide with coupling holes in mirrors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Combined cavities containing waveguide and open parts find a use in submillimetre (SMM) optically pumped lasers (OPL). We examined new methods of transverse modes selection in a resonator based on circular metal waveguide with homogeneous mirrors. However, it is possible to implement a potentially broad band of working wavelengths of SMM OPL only by the use of a wide band coupler in the cavity. Transverse modes of wide-band combined cavity SMM OPL with holes in mirrors are explored both theoretically and experimentally.

articleTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: laser cavity resonators; semiconductor lasers; solid lasers; laser pumping; dye lasers; gas lasers; excimer lasers; laser mirrors; laser tuning; optical fibre communication; vortices; nonlinear optics; and integrated optics.

articleTitle: Adaptive optics for laser beam control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: This paper presents the novel adaptive optical closed loop system (ACLS) for compensation of the laser beam aberrations and results of its application in high power lasers. A closed-loop adaptive algorithm is developed to control for deformable bimorph mirror. The control voltages applied to all electrodes reduce the wavefront variations measured by a Hartmann-Shack wavefront sensor (SHWS). Adaptive system can correct for the low-order aberrations in the real-time - the frequency of corrected aberrations is 25 (30) Hz. The amplitude of such aberrations - about 7 microns. It is shown also the successful application of the developed ACLS for correction of aberration of different kinds of lasers.

articleTitle: Measurement of small particles sizes: inverse problem of radiation scattering theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: It is often necessary to measure the size of small particles in different fields of science and technology. These particles can be solid or fluid aerosols in atmosphere, emulsion and suspension in fluid, bacteria, cells in biological objects, etc. For the particles with the sizes between 10 nm and 100 /spl mu/m it is convenient to use measurement methods, which are based on measuring the characteristics of light, which is scattered by these particles. The mathematical problems, which are necessary to solve, are the inverse optics problems. That is, it is required to find object parameters by using the results of the radiation interaction with the object.

articleTitle: Scattering of laser wave beam by anisotropic chiral layer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The problem of laser wave beam scattering by an anisotropic chiral layer is solved via a Fourier spectral method. Polarization transformation of the reflected electromagnetic wave caused by chirality and anisotropy as well as distortion of the reflected field spatial distribution are investigated.

articleTitle: New concept of multipass resonators for gas and solid-state lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Recently we, have offered a relatively new concept of creation of steady multipass resonators for lasers with large volume of active media. This concept was proved in details in our research and developments of CO/sub 2/ lasers with transversal RF pumping. In the present work the results of numerical modeling of such resonators are given. It has been investigated the stability of such resonators is designed at various geometry, their sensitivity to misalignments, the losses for various types of modes, opportunity of various laser transitions or mode selection and so on. The high sensitivity of the laser output characteristics to parameters of lateral reflectors is shown. In the present work it is offered the qualitatively new approach to create the active elements and resonators for compact solid-state lasers with diode pumping on the basis of the same idea.. A lot of new schemes of lasers is discussed, as well as the results of experimental investigations of a microchip Tm:YAlO/sub 3/ diode pumped laser with the cw output power up to 0.5 W and a slope efficiency up to 40%.

articleTitle: Spontaneous and carrier noise in mode-locked hybrid soliton pulse source
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The effect of spontaneous and carrier noise on mode-locked hybrid soliton pulse source (HSPS) is described by coupled-mode equations, and relative intensity noise (RIN) is calculated using numerical solutions of these equations. It is found that transform limited pulses are not generated because of these noises.

articleTitle: Mathematical simulation of conversion of femtosecond pulses to second harmonic in photonic bandgaps
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Summary form only given. We present the results of numerical simulations of the second harmonic generation (SHG) in photonic band gaps (PBG) structures with GaAs/AlAs and GaAs/fused quartz quarter-wave layers under of femtosecond pulse pump. The electromagnetic field inside the slab is presented as a sum of counterpropagating pump and doubled frequency waves. The theoretical consideration is based on the second-order space differential equations for pump and nonlinear transformation waves amplitudes. Simulations of propagating in nonlinear medium are performed by using of method of characteristics. Numerical solution of the equations system was realised by means of fast Fourier transform permitting to take into Account a modification of radiation spectrum after nonlinear transformation of ultrashort pulse. The transmission and reflection coefficients and the density of the optical modes defined as value of the reciprocal group. velocity are calculated. Conversion efficiency reflected and transmitted waves and pulse duration are analysed as a function of the structure period and pump intensity. We show that the value of transmission and reflection coefficients gives a relation between transmitted and reflected waves of the second harmonic whereas the value of the optical modes density determines the nonlinear conversion efficiency. The reflected SHG exceeds transmitted wave for: the PBG GaAs/AlAs more then 30 times. but in the case of PBG GaAs/quartz the intensities of transmitted and reflected pulses were practically identical. The maximum of total conversion efficiency in the both cases occurs for ten periods, and its value is about three percents for pump intensity 400 GW/cm/sup 2/ (PBG GaAs/AlAs). The durations of SHG pulses is less then pump pulses durations in 1//spl radic/2.

articleTitle: Measuring of micrometer diameters of focused laser radiation by bolometer from thin-wire
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The aim of this paper consists in experimental confirmation of the possibility of micrometer diameter measurement of focused laser radiation by thin-wire bolometers. The bolometer material was platinum, which does not yield to corrosion in a wide temperature interval, has a melting point of 1769 /spl deg/C and displays a smooth temperature dependence of the basic physical parameters (temperature coefficient of resistance, factor of absorption efficiency, specific heat, thermal conductivity and coefficient of heat exchange with environment), which determine the transformation coefficient of the bolometer. The thin-wire platinum bolometer had a diameter of 3 microns and a length 8.4 mm.

articleTitle: Combination of Bragg and nonlinear phenomena in open periodic waveguiding structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Physical effects of the monochromatic plane wave scattering on nonlinear films with periodic spatial perturbation of the surface impedance. are theoretically considered., Conditions' of excitations of two surface waves propagating in opposite directions are, found. It is shown that if nonlinear and spatial perturbations have the same infinitesimal order it is necessary to take into consideration the back action of higher harmonics on amplitudes of surface waves. Influence of the Bragg conditions mismatch on frequency characteristics of the higher harmonics amplitudes is investigated. Optimal values of period and amplitude of spatial periodic perturbation,for the higher frequency harmonics. generation are obtained for some values of nonlinear perturbation.

articleTitle: Influence of radiator parameters on tuning characteristics of dye lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The subject of the work presented is the investigation of the dependencies of the dye laser (DL) tuning characteristics on the radiator parameters for the purpose of increasing the efficiency of the DL spectrum tuning in the given wavelength range. To solve the problem the theoretical. and experimental investigations have been made of the dependencies of the tuning band and generation energy of the rhodamine 6G DL on the concentration of dye, length of active medium and spectral characteristics of the reflection coefficient of the resonator output mirror.

articleTitle: Developments in optical resonator parameter measurement towards realising metre
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: There is good potential accuracy in precision interferometry. In order to obtain its total realization there is necessity to obtain a good accuracy for mirror curvature radius from 1 part in 10/sup 6/ to 1 part in 10/sup 7/. In order to achieve this aim we have developed an interferometric method of measuring of mirror radius of curvature. In accordance with this method of checking; a concave mirror and reference plate mirror are combined with a Fabry-Perot interferometer whose length is less than the mirror curvature radius.

articleTitle: T-wave of coaxial waveguide diffraction by semi-infinite system of azimuth slots
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The diffraction problem of coaxial waveguide main mode (T-wave) by periodic system of the axial slots has been investigated. The investigation based on the de- cision of two key-problems. The first key problem is the diffraction problem of coaxial waveguide T-mode by a single axial slot, and the second key problem is the problem of determination of reflecting factor (in a case of multimode it is an operator) of semi-infinite periodic system of axial slots. The mathematical simulation of reflection and transmission. factors value has been realized.

articleTitle: Parametric zonal method of effects regularities simulation in quantum systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The offered combined method of research allows studying more precisely interaction laws of oscillatory systems with pumping. The combined method allows new laws of interactions which allow finding out analytically very difficultly or absolutely impossible.

articleTitle: Increasing a pulse repetition rate of laser with pumping environment passive Q-modulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: One of the ways a pulse repetition rate can increase with decreasing relaxation time is in a high energy level passive modulator, which one can achieve by a passive environment pumping application. For a passive modulation processes analysis, we use a probabilistic method of the description, which is one of the simplest and most precise methods of processes analysis in systems, where it is necessary to allow for the behavior of a large amount of particles (laser).

articleTitle: Possibility of high-frequency pulse discharge application for excimer laser pumping
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: In high-frequency discharges of a capacity type (HFE), more often the HF voltage is applied to plane-parallel electrodes. The electrodes can adjoin to discharge and can be isolated from it by a solid dielectric. In this sense we shall name conditionally. HFE discharges as electrode or electrodeless. In stationary HF discharges all investigations will usually be carried out on the most used frequency For us pulse discharges, having much total features with stationary HFE discharges, is represented the greatest interest. Therefore basic regularity proper to HFE discharges are easier to analyze at first in a stationary case. At first we shall not make accent only on high-pressure discharges, and consider discharges of average pressure for laser technique.

articleTitle: New types of planar waveguides for an integrated optics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: A method of synthesis of planar metal-dielectric lightguides (MDLG) is proposed. The method is connected with restitution of a law of a refractive index changes in a cross-section of a lightguide for a given power localization coefficient of a propagated wave at a fixed frequency. The single-mode and low-mode regimes are assumed. The obtained lightguides, due to their parameters, have potential for various integrated optics devices, e.g. multi-channel waveguide splitters, modulators and switches, filters, and radiating structures.

articleTitle: Numerical simulations of 2-D vertical cavity surface emitting laser arrays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Modal behavior of a 2-D (square lattice geometry) antiguided vertical cavity surface emitting laser (VCSEL) array was studied by 3-D bidirectional beam propagation method. The VCSEL array is made by periodical transverse variation of resonance frequency of a local cavity formed by Bragg reflectors and active layer. Using a method based on functions of Krylov's subspace, a number of array optical modes were found for different spacing lengths between elements and a size of the array. In calculations, both Fourier and space variable descriptions of beam propagation were combined. The FFT technique was used for calculations of the Fourier image and the original. Array optical modes having different symmetry properties were found. They include in-phase mode with constant phase over the array, out-of-phase mode with alternating phase between elements and modes with mixed symmetry. 4/spl times/4 and 10/spl times/10 laser arrays were studied numerically. Conditions are found for favorable lasing of the in-phase mode providing high laser beam quality.

articleTitle: Fiber-optical vortices: physical properties and applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The aim of our paper is to elucidate the main problems of singular optics of free space and homogeneous isotropic media and to consider the topics of the vortex behavior in guiding inhomogeneous media both subjected to various perturbations and in the steady-state.

articleTitle: Fast photonic network modelling with new wavelet method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: Pulse propagation in a nonlinear optical medium is described by the nonlinear Schrodinger equation. For large wavelength division multiplexing systems, the simulation time can run into weeks. We developed a new, flexible, fast and adaptive split-step wavelet collocation method (SSWCM). Using a set of compactly supported basis functions with cardinal property, the SSWCM has the complexity O(N). This is superior to the complexity O(N log/sub 2/ N) of the standard split-step Fourier method, and provides a substantial speed-up for large N.

articleTitle: Application of thermal, laser and ionizing radiation conditioning for quality improvement of KDP and DKDP single crystals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: The investigation carried out on the industrial crystals and analysis of the works of the different authors show that any choice of one or another method for the improvement of the qualities of the KH/sub 2/PO/sub 4/ (KDP) and KD/sub 2/PO/sub 4/ (DKDP) crystals depends on the specific application of the crystals and the types of defects in the crystals. The thermal conditioning can be effectively used for recovering optical transparency of gamma, X-ray, or UV irradiated crystals. The thermal and laser conditioning methods improving laser damage threshold are effective for the crystals used for the frequency, conversion of the high-intensive laser radiation. It is necessary to use the ionizing radiation conditioning method for the crystals worked.. at the ionizing irradiation conditions.

articleTitle: Measurement of polarization and applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of LFNM 2002. 4th International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling (IEEE Cat. No.02EX549)
abstract: We present a polarization measuring system which is capable to determine the complete, Stokes vector of radiation with a wavelength from deep ultraviolet (i.e. 190 nm) to the visible spectral range. Due to a special design the entire wavelength range is covered by one single device (i.e. no exchange of optical components is necessary). In addition the system is able to determine the Jones and the Mueller matrices of lenses, waveplates and other samples automatically and spatially resolved within the same wavelength region. The system consists of a polarization state generator and a polarization sensitive detector consisting of a rotating waveplate, a polarizer, and a detector. A fast Fourier algorithm provides the four Stokes parameters of the light where all parameters are calculated independently. By tuning the polarization of the illuminating light we calculate the Jones matrix and the birefringence of the sample. Under industrial conditions we found an accuracy of the stress birefringence of 0.1 nm and an accuracy of the azimuth of the fast axis of 0.1/spl deg/. Because polarization is a very important property of radiation, the system has a lot of applications. Examples are the testing of optical elements like waveplates, polarizers and lens system.
